newsitem.title: UK: Shell N. Sea Teal fields to reach peak by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Shell N. Sea Teal fields to reach peak by year-end.

text.p: The Teal area in the central North Sea will reach peak oil production of about 60,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of this year, a Shell Expro official said on Friday.
The development, which consists of three oil and gas fields -- Guillemot A, Teal and Teal South -- came on stream on October 5.
Shell Expro, operator in the British sector of the North Sea for the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Exxon Corp Corp, said crude was being pumped via the Anasuria floating production vessel.
"As of today Teal is producing about 24,000 bpd and should average 14,000 bpd for October," said the official.
The fields, which lie 150 km east of Aberdeen in blocks 21/25 and 21/30, have been tapped by satellite wells tied back to subsea manifolds, in turn tied back to the Anasuria.
Oil will be exported by Shell Expro's central North Sea tanker fleet.
Gas will be exported via the Fulmar line to St Fergus, once production begins.
